utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Good morning to everybody in and around the courtroom. I am sure that we will find a solution about the question we have discussed yesterday, but we should discuss that in the presence of the witness in private session. And, therefore, the witness should be brought in, please. Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Lord's peace upon this house, and let the outcome be determined by the providence. My proposal is that the next session we begin with the video footage about the events that the witness described, and then I will proceed with my questions without mentioning any names. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much for that. Good morning, sir. Welcome back to the courtroom. I have to remind you that the affirmation to tell the truth you made at the beginning of your testimony yesterday still applies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We have to discuss a procedural matter and we turn into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are back in open session, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Tolimir, please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Once again, Lord's peace on this house. And let the outcome of this trial be decided by providence, not by my wishes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My greetings to Mr. Skrbic. And I wish him a pleasant stay amongst us.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please now have in e-court 1D1063. I'm -- apology. 1D1115. It's an expert report. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: You see here: "Ratko Skrbic's Expert Report on Srebrenica and Zepa." That's the title of the report. My question is: Are you the author of this report? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. My next question is: Have you compiled this report on your own? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, completely on my own.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. My third question is: Has anyone suggested to you to include any conclusions that are contained in the report as it is?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Please, Mr. Skrbic, can you tell the Chamber which specific sources you used when compiling this report. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: While drafting this report, I used combat documents of the 28th Division, of the 285th Brigade, the 2nd Corps of the ABH, and the General Staff of the ABH. In addition to that, I relied on witness statements regardless of whether they were from amongst the Muslim ranks or from international forces that were deployed in Srebrenica at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Skrbic. We don't need to go through the entire report, because that would be a time-consuming exercise. I am going only to deal with specific issues, and therefore can you please tell us how you understood the situation to be that preceded the attacks -- or, rather, the attack on the Srebrenica enclave?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My understanding of the situation is contained in the fact that in the Zepa and Srebrenica enclaves, throughout the whole conflict in Bosnia-Herzegovina, there was conflict ongoing all the time between the 28th Division of the ABH and the Drina Corps of the VRS. Based on such an understanding of the situation, I drafted my report in such a manner that would allow one to have an insight of the conflict between the two armies.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Please, during that period, i.e., in 1995, do you know what was the situation between the conflicting parties, and did those activities have any impact on the events that took place? Did you incorporate that into your report?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I stated in my report the fact that that was a mutual conflict, which by nature it is, and that the units of the 28th Division were permanently involved in combat operations launched from within the enclave against the Drina Corps units on the edges of the enclave and sometimes targeting Serbian villages on the edges of the enclave where there were no VRS troops. Therefore, I understood it to be that the VRS was no longer in a position to tolerate such attacks and such operations, and it was bound for the purpose of protecting both their men and the population to react. It was its principal role.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Skrbic. Can you please tell the Chamber how many enclaves existed in the territory of Republika Srpska according to what you know.

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to what I know, there were the following enclaves: Srebrenica, Zepa, Gorazde, Bihac, and Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you identify some problems that were kind of common denominator for all the enclaves that you mentioned? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The fact that the term "demilitarised zone" is being constantly used, there is an understanding that this term did not reflect the actual situation at the time. It is not possible to send combat documents and carry out combat operations from a demilitarised zone. It is also impossible to have units such as divisions, brigade, or even corps deployed in demilitarised zone. If there were such units involved in combat operations, then one cannot qualify them as demilitarised zones.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Was your unit targeted by attacks from demilitarised zone, and what can you tell us about it?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Only I have to add that that was on a smaller scale than in other demilitarised zones, because my brigade was made up of the people who had been expelled from Bihac and its surrounding, they had many relatives who remained behind in Bihac and probably that was the reason that they were unwilling to become involved in fierce fighting. That was a specific feature of my unit, but we indeed were attacked several times from the demilitarised zone. For example, in October 1994 they carried out a large-scale attack and they managed to push us back to a number of kilometres from Petrovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Were there any such attacks launched from a Bihac demilitarised zone in 1995, where you were deployed as a defence force? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These operations were stepped-up in 1995, not only in time but also in strength, and they were consistent with an all-out operation carried out by the Croatian army who, at the time, was involved in preparing significant plans that would solve the question of the Serbian Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Could you tell us whether from that demilitarised zone your territory that you defended was attacked, and to what extent were there attacks launched from that demilitarised zone on areas in Republika Srpska, and what was the distance between the demilitarised zone and the places on which attacks were launched?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to say, again, that as a professional soldier I have problems with the term "demilitarised zone," given that such zones contained corps, for example, which launched fierce attacks on the VRS in the area, so I would be grateful if I didn't have to use the term "demilitarised zone" in order to refer to areas where units were present.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Skrbic. I am asking about this so that we can see what sort of areas received the status of a demilitarised zone. So I'm asking you to tell us the following: Bihac had the status it had; were any attacks launched from Bihac against your brigade, and how long did the breakthrough last, the breakthrough of forces from Bihac to the territory of Republika Srpska in 1995? And what distance are we talking about?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, units of the ABiH 5th Corps did launch an attack on my unit, amongst others. It was between the 13th and 14th of January, 1995, that my unit was attacked, and that was the beginning of a large-scale offensive launched by the Muslim armed forces in the territory of Republika Srpska together with HVO units and Croatian army units. In 1995, this attack lasted until Sanski Most was taken, and that location is about 80 kilometres away from Bihac.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Skrbic. Yesterday you told us what the distance was between Srebrenica and Nezuk. Can you repeat that distance, please? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The distance is about 60 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. If forces from Bihac were armed and could reach Sanski Most, which is 80 kilometres into the territory of Republika Srpska, then could forces from Srebrenica cover a distance of 60 kilometres by breaking through under arms? Was this possible for them? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The forces of the 28th Division, when they decided to break through in the direction of Tuzla, could in fact do so. As far as I can remember, I explained this yesterday, but I'll repeat what I said: They could do this because on the axis of the breakthrough the VRS didn't have sufficient units to prevent that breakthrough and to neutralise the 28th Division, so the 28th Division was able to break through and did so.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Skrbic. Have you found in international law that a demilitarised zone managed to carry out such a breakthrough into a territory from which it obtained the status of a demilitarised zone? Have you ever come across such a thing in international law? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I never came across any such thing. But I know that no units should really take action from demilitarised zones. If a zone is demilitarised, then it's demilitarised. That means that it doesn't have any military or paramilitary units on its territory, and there is no combat in such zones or there shouldn't be any such combat.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Was there a demilitarised zone in Bosnia in accordance with the standards and regulations of International War Law? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there wasn't a single demilitarised zone.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Skrbic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we see 1D1070, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Skrbic. In front of us we have a document from the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. It's from the staff of the Supreme Command of the OS of the Republic of BH, the date of the 15th of November, 1994. The name of the document is "Regrouping and Resubordination." It's addressed to the 2nd Corps, the OG-8 Srebrenica, the 1st Zepa Brigade, and the Eastern Bosnia Operations Group Gorazde. Please, this document or order, does it refer to something that a military expert would be interested in, would it draw your attention to it? What sort of a document is this, in other words?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an order in which the ABiH is, in fact, being organised in demilitarised or protected zones, the zones of Gorazde, Srebrenica, and Zepa. It is important from the point of view of the fact that the army is being reorganised with the objective of strengthening the 28th Division, first of all; secondly, to subordinate the 285th Brigade in Zepa to the division, because up until that point in time it was either part of the Gorazde's operation group, but it was also independent or received orders as an independent unit quite frequently; and finally, the final objective of the reorganising the army is to increase its efficiency and to increase the efficiency of command and control.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you tell us why the subordination of the Zepa Brigade was, in fact, defined in this manner?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to my understanding of the situation, this was done because they wanted to establish links between the Zepa and Srebrenica enclaves. These two enclaves were to form a single enclave.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Skrbic, could you please tell us whether on the basis of this document a system of command and control was established from Srebrenica and Zepa, and in both zones, was this done by the Main Staff of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If the Supreme Command Staff ordered the subordination of the 285th Brigade to the 28th Division, it means that as of that date, the date on which this order on the subordination was -- resubordination was issued, that unit became part of the 28th Division and received tasks and orders from the command of the 28th Division. In addition, the command of the 28th Division would synchronise and co-ordinate actions together with that brigade and it would assign tasks to that brigade to that effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Skrbic. Please, you can see that the document's date is the 15th of November, 1994. So could you please tell us whether this is a document that proves that the Zepa, Gorazde, and Srebrenica demilitarised zones were always armed and that the command of the Supreme Command Staff was involved in the reorganisation of the army and was involved in organising the army for attacks that were to be launched from those demilitarised zones? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course. That's what it means, because those demilitarised zones were never demilitarised. The 28th Division was never dismantled, the 28-- the 285th Brigade was never dismantled, the operative group in Gorazde was never dismantled either, and so on and so forth. So they continued to be armed and they had their military units.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I have to remind both speakers to slow down. It was very fast again, and the interpreters and the court reporter have some problems. And please don't overlap. And wait for the end of the translation. Please carry on, Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Skrbic. Mr. Skrbic, have you come across documents that show that international forces deployed in the protected zones had information according to which these demilitarised zones were armed? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I had a number of such documents. And I can now mention just one of the documents from General Ridderstad [phoen], from the UNPROFOR command for north-east in Tuzla. He addressed the command of the 28th Division or perhaps the command of the 2nd Corps. I think it was the command of the 2nd Corps. And he said that he knew - that's what it says in the document - he knew that demilitarisation was never in fact carried out.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Skrbic. Since you were in the Bihac demilitarised zone or linked to that zone, could you provide us with any information that shows that UN forces had knowledge about the combat units in the military zone -- or in the demilitarise zone, Bihac, and had information on their activities, the action taken against the territory in the Republika Srpska as well as actions taken against your brigade and your corps?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Naturally I had such information. I also had my own personal experience. In the 2nd Krajina Corps I had a so called hot-line with the commander of the French Battalion in Bihac. Whenever there was an attack launched from the Bihac protected zone, an attack against our units, and on my unit, I would always speak to the commander of the French Battalion. We would meet. We in fact met on a number of occasions, and I would ask him to prevent that if at all possible. UNPROFOR knew that the ABiH was taking action from demilitarised zones and was then returning to those zones that were under UNPROFOR protection or the protection of the UN forces.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please see 1D-- or could 1D1070 please be admitted into evidence. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Yes, it will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document shall be assigned Exhibit D352. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we now please show the witness the following document, 1D1073. Thank you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: We can now see the document in front of us. From the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Srebrenica municipality, municipal defence secretariat, dated the 9th of March, 1994. It's a report on recruitment and replenishment of materiel supplies for the armed forces and other recruitment beneficiaries. It was addressed to the district defence secretariat, Tuzla, and it was signed by the secretary, National Defence Secretariat Professor Suljo Hasanovic. Could you please tell us why this document is important for the Defence? Why did you examine it, and in what manner did you in fact examine in it your expert report? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document is important, above all, because the date is after the signing of the agreement on demilitarisation, and then in the document itself we can see that units are still being brought up to strength. Bringing units up to strength is the responsibility of the Ministry of Defence. These are defence secretariats in Tuzla, in Srebrenica municipality, and this report is being sent on bringing units up to strength so that units of the 28th Division could be brought up to strength as planned in subsequent events. The secretariat in Tuzla also had to take into account the need for bringing up to strength other bodies within the system of defence and replenishing supplies as well. Bringing units up to strength is done only when you are planning to use units, because otherwise there would be no sense in bringing units up to strength and in replenishing units with equipment. There would be no objective if these units were not to carry out combat activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Skrbic. Please, if we look at the bullet points, we will see that under 1 it says that: "A total of 5.254 conscripts are deployed in the armed forces..." My question is this: Are these the armed forces of Bosnia and Herzegovina or perhaps of a region or perhaps of a unit? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document refers to the 28th Division and recruiting fighters for the 28th Division in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Under the other bullet points, the term "conscript" is abbreviated to "V/O." Can you please explain for the benefit of the Trial Chamber the meaning of the abbreviation "V/O"? because we don't have the adequate translation in the English language. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We have an English translation in front of us on the screen.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. In every bullet point except the first one it says "V/O"; only in the first bullet point it says "conscript." Since from then on the word -- the term "conscript" is abbreviated into "V/O," I wanted the witness to explain the abbreviation "V/O" and tell us what that means. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is an abbreviation that was inherited from the JNA. It means conscript.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Skrbic. Can you explain to the Trial Chamber what does it mean to be a military conscript? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That means that all able-bodied males are registered with the secretariat for defence. They are subject to the obligation of being sent to the units when the units need to be brought up to strength. They are also subject to the obligation to be sent to units of work obligation, units of civilian protection, and other units, not only of army units. A military conscript is any male of age up to the age of 64. The secretariat makes sure that the fittest males are sent to army units and the others are sent to the units of work obligation and civilian protection.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Skrbic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I would like to tender 1D1073 into evidence. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document shall be assigned Exhibit D353. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. And now I would like to call up 1D1097. Thank you. I would like to thank the e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: And now, Mr. Skrbic, this is a document issued by the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina of the 2nd Corps command. It was drafted in Tuzla on the 18th of January, 1995, and it was sent to Operations Group 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, and 8. Can you please tell us whether you saw this document before; and if you did, what kind of a document is it? What is it about? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document is another proof that the 2nd Corps of the BiH army, pursuant to an order of the staff of the Supreme Command, was engaged in the reorganisation of the military. The reorganisation of the units of the 2nd Corps meant only one thing, and that was an attempt to increase the efficiency of those units and the system of command and control in those units. We can see that the exercise to reorganise the army was carried out after the agreement on demilitarisation was signed, which is yet another proof that demilitarisation was never carried out and that the agreement on demilitarisation was never complied with. I apologise, may I be allowed to say something else?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, it is in your hands.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Skrbic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Skrbic. I interrupted you. If you wish to do so, you may continue and complete your answer. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just wanted to add that in this order we can see that this is not only about reorganising the existing units but also about establishing new ones. As you can see under bullet point 1, several new units were to be established according to a plan in an organised manner and with a purpose.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Skrbic. Can you please tell us: When this document was drafted, did the warring parties have any obligation towards each other?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the time when there should have been a complete cease-fire pursuant to an agreement signed on the 31st December, 1994. This, in other words, means that this agreement on truce or cease-fire was not complied with fully. Instead, it -- an opportunity was taken to improve the efficiency of the army and to reorganise it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Skrbic. To cut a long story short, let me ask you whether you included this document into your expert report on pages 19 and 17 and 18 in Serbian and English respectively?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would kindly ask the e-court to display the pages that I have just referred to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We need the document number.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D115. Thank you. Actually, there should be three numbers 1 and then 5, and all that following 1D; in other words, 1D1115. Thank you. I would like to thank the e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Mr. Skrbic, I apologise for not having displayed your expert report prior to asking you about it. I have another question: Can you please explain the purpose of the organisational changes that took place in so many units in so many operative groups?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were several reasons to do that: The first one was mainstreaming; the second one was improving efficiency of the 2nd Corps, including the newly established 28th Division.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Skrbic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to call up page 2, and the document number is 1D1097. Thank you. I would also like to call up page 3 in the English version of the same document.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Skrbic. Again, there are some abbreviations, standing up for operative groups, and then we have numbers 1, 2, 4, 6, 7. Can you please tell us which of the units made up the 2nd Corps which reorganised its OGs, and what units were on the strength of the 28th Division? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The units of the 2nd Corps, after the reorganisation, are listed in the document. I don't want to waste any time on them. And the units of the 28th Division were actually brigades that pre-existed the reorganisation, and the only addition was the 285th Brigade from Zepa; in other words, OGs were re-established into divisions. They were reorganised to become divisions to facilitate command, control, and management of the units during combat.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Skrbic. Does that mean that those divisions were to be directly subordinated to the corps command from then onwards? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Skrbic, can you please tell us something about the newly established war unit, the 28th Division, because you say the duration of mobilisation 12 hours, the -- in charge of the plan of mobilisation, the 28th Division. What does that mean? That's on the following page of the text in Serbian, paragraph 2. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the e-court please display that paragraph after I have put my question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is customary in a military that when a superior command establishes a new unit it determines and defines its location, the duration of mobilisation. And the duration of mobilisation can be anything from several hours to 24 or even 48 hours, and that usually depends on the role and the significance of that particular unit on the strength of the higher ranking formation. Here we can see that in the 28th Division the duration of the mobilisation was to be 20 hours. That means that from the moment when an order was issued to mobilise troops and to bring the unit up to strength, within 20 hours the unit has to be complete and ready to be deployed in combat. It is also customary for the commander of the unit to be in charge of the mobilisation plan, and that's how the order was drafted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Skrbic. Above the text that we have just read and that you commented upon, there are the numbers of the brigades. What brigades are those, and does it mean that the 28th Division will be in charge of their mobilisation plans? Does this mean that these brigades are the units of the 28th Division? Is that confirmed by the document?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, these brigades are the units of the 28th Division, and the same procedure is followed with regard to mobilisation. So whatever the 28th Division received from the 2nd Corps by way of an order, the same order was elaborated by the 28th Division and sent to its subordinated units, and this order was followed down to the lowest-ranking units, i.e., companies.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Skrbic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With the president's leave, can I have this document 1D1097 be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document shall be assigned Exhibit D354. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Mr. Skrbic, please, in your report you addressed the issue of supplies provided to the ABH in Srebrenica and Zepa. Can you explain what kind of supplies were delivered to the army in Srebrenica and Zepa and in what way?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The units deployed in Srebrenica and Zepa enclaves was predominantly carried out by helicopters but also by land routes. They were delivered from the helidrome or helipad to the subordinate units of the 28th Division.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Skrbic. Did you have in mind here only specific supplies or did you refer to all materiel and equipment required by the troops in Srebrenica and Zepa in general?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I speak about supplies provided to units, I mean by that they are supplied with weapons, munition, and other lethal assets required for conducting combat operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Skrbic. Tell us, What kind of lines of supplies exists within the provisions of the military doctrine?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, the supplies that come from own production, provided a state has its own military industry or complex; the second source is by importing these assets from other countries; and another sort is war booty. So these are the most common ways of supplying an army with all the necessary assets, and, of course, included into this should be the communications devices.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us something about how these supplies were actually delivered?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Delivery is the term that means that a superior command provides the necessary supplies to its subordinate units in the manner available. That is the substance of the term "delivery." Delivery is carried out up to the point which is safe for those who carry the supplies, and from there it is distributed to subordinate units.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Skrbic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have in e-court document 1D445. Thank you. I will repeat the number: 1D445. Thank you. Obviously we have some problems. The document perhaps hasn't been uploaded or it cannot be found.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, perhaps it was uploaded but not released to the Registry and the Prosecution. I see Mr. Gajic is checking the situation with the document. Mr. Gajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, in my e-court this document is available, and it had been uploaded a long time ago. Therefore, I propose that we move to the next question and then we will come back to this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It is not necessary. I am optimistic. Now we have it on the screen. It's there. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. My thanks to e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Mr. Skrbic, what we see here is a report by the Zepa Brigade, dated 31st December, 1994, sent to the staff of the Supreme Command of the Armed Forces of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina in Kakanj, attention Brigadier-General Enver Hadzihasanovic, and signed by the commander Colonel Avdo Palic. I will briefly read this, and I quote: [As read] "We have done everything pursuant to your order, and we were quite successfully in that. The cargo has been offloaded quickly, it was relocated to a safe location, and all the traces were removed. UNPROFOR saw our helicopter on the entry point to the zone and reported to their commander in Zepa that in the vicinity of Zlovrh three helicopters SS landed, and that was probably due because they were observed circling before the landing. I have undertaken all the measures to prevent UNPROFOR from doing anything that would be unfavorable for us, and I will inform you accordingly when the time comes for that." Mr. Skrbic, is this one of the document that you relied upon when you gave answers to my previous questions when you mentioned helicopter deliveries of supplies? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It not only corroborates my claim that supplies were provided by helicopters but also my claim that that supplies were delivered, and you can see in the document that they received the assets very quickly and that they had already been distributed to subordinate units. He also says that he was having problems with UNPROFOR because he anticipates that UNPROFOR might intervene in order to prevent helicopter flights. For that reason he made an effort to thwart UNPROFOR in any way possible in their attempt to prevent and stop any deliveries and supplies.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, please, in the second paragraph, line two, it reads: "Was Brigadier Oric, Naser, notified that he should be -- he should send his men as soon as possible to Zepa pursuant to previous orders? And if not, inform him about everything."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the accused please now repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, the interpreters ask you to repeat your question. We have on the record your quotation from the document, but the question is missing.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: My question was: Mr. Skrbic, was this cargo, delivered by three helicopters, intended solely for Zepa?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not solely for the needs of the Zepa Brigade. In this specific case, we have supplies delivered to the 28th Division. But in order to secure the safety of helicopter flights, they have chosen a heliport in the Zepa area because for pilots that was the safest place where they could fly, land, and offload the cargo. And that's why he's asking whether Brigadier Naser Oric had been notified, because he was supposed to come and collect the assets for other units of the 28th Division. And what was intended to -- for the 285th Brigade, it had already been taken by the commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Skrbic, in the last paragraph that I quoted, it says that: "He should send his men to Zepa pursuant to the previous orders ..." My question is: Can you tell us whether the command of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina had already been involved in co-ordinating matters between various levels that were privy to the deliveries for Zepa and Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This can mean only one thing and that is that supplies were being provided on a continual basis, even before this event, and some documents indicate that they went on after. So the units of the 28th Division were being supplied with the necessary assets on a regular basis.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, please carry on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I would like to tender document 1D445 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It will be marked for identification pending translation, but we have to wait for the return of the Court Officer. There is something he has to deal with and he will come back soon. Please carry on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I would like to call up the next document, with your leave, and that is 1D451. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Mr. Skrbic, this is yet another document produced by the 1st Zepa Light Brigade on the 9th of January, 1995, and the document is also addressed to the General Staff, attention Brigadier-General Hadzihasanovic, and it was sent by the commander of the Zepa Brigade Colonel Avdo Palic. And here we can see the specification of the assets required, and I quote: "If it is possible for you to provide another delivery of materiel and equipment by helicopters, please send us the following as priorities: "1. Recoilless gun. "2. Grenades for recoilless gun. "3. RPG-7 launcher. "4. Rockets for RPG-7. "5. Zolja or grenades for hand-held launcher. "7. [as interpreted] Grenades for mortar, 60-millimetre. "7. Ammunition, 7.62-millimetres --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Please slow down. If you look into the transcript, you will see that they are not able to catch everything. Please slow down. And perhaps you start again after number 4. You will see that it's not properly recorded.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I apologise to the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Number 4 is rocket for RPG-7, 15 pieces. Number 5 is Zolja or rocket for a hand-held launcher, at least 30 pieces. Number 6 is a shell for a mortar, 60-millimetre, at least 50 pieces. Number 7: ammunition, 7.62-millimetres times 39, and 7.9 times 7.62 [as interpreted] for sub-machine gun and M-84 machine-gun; and he also needs pistol ammunition 7.62- and 7.65-millimetres. Number 8: rifle grenades, shape-charged and contact-action ones, at least 50 pieces. Number 9: hand-grenade, at least 100 pieces. Number 10: mine detector, at least three pieces. Number 11: automatic rifles, at least 50 pieces. Number 12: light machine-gun, M-84, at least three pieces. Number 3. [as interpreted] amateur radio set, one. Number 14: a small generator. Number 15: a powerful accumulator, two pieces ..." and so on and so forth. Mr. Skrbic, could you comment on the amount of weapons and ammunition that is requested here for the operation? What would such an amount of weapons and ammunition serve for?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to standard military procedure, apart from establishing priority tasks you also establish what sort of equipment should be given priority. Here it is quite clearly seen that equipment for armed combat has been given priority. Initially it might seem that the equipment requested is not a significant amount. However, if we bear in mind the terrain where operations are taken in Zepa and in the 28th Division area, then this equipment is quite sufficient for the purpose of defending the enclave but also for the purpose of carrying out active combat outside the enclaves. This is a period which is also after the signed cease-fire, and this shows that the cease-fire that was signed is being used by the 28th Division to equip itself and train itself for forthcoming action. I cannot now remember exactly who said this, but I do remember that it was said that it's stupid to have an army and not to use it. And this could mean in this case, too, that if you have units which are being equipped with these supplies, one should expect this equipment to be used in combat activity.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Skrbic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, could this document 1D451 please be admitted into evidence until we find a translation. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It will be marked for identification pending translation.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter document 1D445 shall be assigned Exhibit D355, marked for identification. And the 65 ter document 1D451 shall be assigned Exhibit D356, marked for identification pending translation. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Both documents are pending translation. Thank you. Mr. Tolimir, I assume that you will move to another document or topic now. I was informed, in the meantime, that in the Detention Unit there was a problem with water, a leakage somewhere, and therefore during the break I hope we will receive a report if that relates to your cell in any way. The Court Officer will inform the Chamber and especially you, Mr. Tolimir, and the other party which measures have to be taken. We should have our first break now, and during the break I hope everything will be resolved. Or, at least, we will receive reports how to proceed further. If there is no other information by the Chamber, we will assume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The Chamber is informed that the problem in the Detention Unit was resolved in the meantime. I hope you have received this message too, Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It was my misunderstanding. It is not related to the Detention Unit, but to the holding cells here in the building of the Tribunal. In that case, we can proceed, and you may continue with your examination-in-chief, Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Could we now see the following document: 1D1088. Thank you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Here we can see a document from the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina from the army General Staff, drafted on the 18th of January, 1995, in Kakanj. It says: Order to the 1st Zepa Mountain Brigade, to Colonel Avdo Palic, personally. Once you'd had a look at it, could you tell us whether this is an answer to Avdo Palic's request in which he requested a certain amount of weapons and materiel? And you commented on that request. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. And customary military procedure was thereby respected. A superior responds to a request from a subordinate for materiel and equipment and provides such materiel and equipment if that is possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Skrbic, please, if you have a look at the addressee, it says: "To Colonel Avdo Palic, personally." What does "n/r" mean?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that means "personally." And only particularly important documents are sent to someone in person. The equipment is more important than the document itself, but to prevent the document from ending up in the wrong hands this mention was made: To Avdo Palic, personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Since the document was sent on the 18th of January by the General Staff and sent to Zepa, please tell me who was involved in arming in Zepa and who was responsible for deliveries? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document is important because deliveries are made by the army General Staff of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina and that is not common practice. The General Staff doesn't usually supply units that are two or even more levels below. Usually the General Staff would provide the 2nd Corps or deliver the second -- deliver the equipment to the 2nd Corps, and then the 2nd Corps would act on the basis of priority tasks and on the basis of the needs of the units. It would then determine how to distribute the equipment. It's also necessary to note that this document has a date subsequent to the signing of the cease-fire agreement, which also shows that the agreement was used in order to supply units.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Skrbic. Could you please tell us whether at the time the no-fly zone ban in Bosnia-Herzegovina was in force? And did that have any effect on the fact that the General Staff was directly involved in deliveries to its own units via air or in other ways? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that resolution didn't have any effect, because supplies were provided through secret channels, through the use of helicopters which flew over the mountains and flew through canyons, so experienced pilots were able to provide supplies in this manner.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Have a look at the date. Was this done at the time when this no-fly zone was in force in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Skrbic. Were there frequent flights to supply Zepa and Srebrenica in spite of the no-fly zone that was supposed to be enforced, and was this noticed by international organisations that monitored the skies above Bosnia? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Naturally, if there were such flights, they had to be noticed because the international forces and the UN forces, together with NATO forces, had all the necessary surveillance equipment in order to be able to detect the flights of helicopters. Helicopter flights were quite frequent right up until June 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Skrbic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could 1D1008 please be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I think this is the wrong number. We are looking at 1D1088, and this will be received into evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document shall be assigned Exhibit D357. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [No interpretation] [microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Your microphone.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I have another question, so could you leave the document on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Mr. Skrbic, does this document show whether the forces in Zepa and Srebrenica had anti-armour weapons at their disposal?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, of course. RPG - rockets - are anti-armour weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Is that under item 6 in this list?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Item 6 is a rocket-launcher. Item number 7 is the missile that is used for the launcher in question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Can hand-held launchers be used for anti-armour combat?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course. Rifle-launched grenades can also be used for such purposes. Shape-charged rifle-launched grenades can be used for such purposes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. We can also see that the delivery of such equipment has been requested here; is that the case or not?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please now see 1D1089. Thank you. I would like to thank the e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Mr. Skrbic, we see another document issued by the Army of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. It was issued by the 1st Zepa Light Brigade on the 19th of January, 1995. It was sent to the army General Staff, personally to Brigadier-General Hadzihasanovic. In this document, the brigadier-general was informed that the load that was sent on the 18th of January was received and stored at a secure location. A request is made for the army to be notified about the arrival of the second load. Does this document prove the point that we were just discussing?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is the answer to the previous document. Subordinated units are duty-bound to report to the superior command about the implementation of any order issued by the superior command.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Skrbic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would kindly ask the Presiding Judge to admit into evidence the document that we see on the screen, which is 1D1089.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document shall be assigned Exhibit D358. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. And now I would kindly ask the e-court to display 1D431. Thank you. Thank you. We are still waiting for it. I repeat the number: 1D431. 1D431, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, Mr. Gajic, I was told that the Defence didn't release it yet. Please check.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I have it in e-court. I don't understand what the problem is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Gajic, perhaps you have it saved in your private Defence folder, but it has to be released to the Registry and the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President, we know that. That document was released a long time ago. I'm convinced, because it was uploaded a long time ago, I'm convinced that it has been released.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Since the document cannot be found, we are going to look at another one, 1D1081.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: During the next break you will be able to discuss the matter with the Registry.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Mr. Skrbic, we can now see a document issued by the Army of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina of its OG-8 in Srebrenica. It was sent on the 3rd November, 1994, to the Brigadier-General Enver Hadzihasanovic, personally. This is an answer to his document 02-1/1347-1. And it says here: "In connection with your memo number," so-and-so, "dated 1 November 1994, we hereby inform you that we too are preparing intensively for the forthcoming operation. We have already sent you our idea for carrying out the task. "We have made contact with the commander of the Zepa Brigade and agreed on carrying out the task of infiltrating materiel and technical equipment via this channel." Please, Mr. Skrbic, tell us, What is this document? Thank you. And what is the comment rate of the first document that is referred to in this document as well as the document that we see on the screen? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this document is the continuation for the preparation of units for combat. Previously, we saw that a resupply was completed, as well as the mainstreaming of the units, and now we can see that the units are preparing for combat. They are informing the superior command about their capabilities. It is to be assumed that the superior command knows what the division's capabilities are; however, it is also obvious that since the division commander sends a dedicated individual to the highest-ranking command to inform them about the unit's capabilities, it is obvious that the operation in the pipeline is very significant. If it wasn't that significant, this envoy from the 28th Division would not be sent to the General Staff to inform the General Staff about the combat capabilities of the division.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Since we're talking about preparations for combat and since Brigadier Naser Oric refers to that and since he sends his personal representative to the staff of the superior command - so the Supreme Command - would say that these are preparations for the activities of the Srebrenica OG directed at units and areas around Srebrenica? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As you can see in the document, the division commander says: "We are also preparing intensively for the forthcoming operation ..." This means that the operation is being prepared by the General Staff, by the 2nd Corps, and that the 28th Division is preparing to participate in the operation from the enclave, because this is the only way they can act from within the enclave against the other units.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Skrbic. This is obviously a co-ordinated activity involving the General Staff and OG-8 under the command of Brigadier Naser Oric. Would you say that plans were made for some joint activities that should have taken place at the same time from two different axes? Is the operative group in the protected area meant to be used for launching attacks from within the protected area?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, I have to say that it is not customary, according to the military procedure and pursuant to the standards of command and control, for the Main Staff to issue orders and tasks to a unit two ranks or two steps below it. However, it is obvious that the operation in question is of particular significance, which is why the Main Staff is the one co-ordinating that operation. The Main Staff knows what the general plan is for the use of the Army of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. And then when the General Staff receives information about the combat capabilities of the 28th Division from the personal envoy of Naser Oric, in keeping with that the General Staff will give its task to that unit. I repeat: This is obviously a very significant task, and the division will certainly act from within the protected area, because within that protected area it does not have anybody to fight.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this document be admitted, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter document 1D1081 shall be assigned Exhibit D359. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I have just been informed that document 1D431 is ready to be used. Therefore, I would kindly ask the e-court to display it, 1D431. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: We can see this document issued by the Army of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, by the command of the Srebrenica OG. It was sent on the 29th of July, 1994. It was sent to the command of the 2nd Corps in Tuzla to the intelligence organ. We are interested in the second paragraph in this document. I am going to read it, and I quote: [As read] "In a conversation with the representatives of UNPROFOR in Srebrenica on the 29th July, 1994, we learnt that the UNPROFOR representatives have been informed about the preparations for a larger-scale combat from the axes of Kladanj, towards Han Pijesak and Vlasenica, and the combat operations will be carried out in the foreseeable future. The representatives of the UN, in a conversation with one of the commanders of the BiH Army who is currently deployed in Kladanj, also learned that in the territory of Kladanj a brigade is being set up and that the population of Vlasenica and Han Pijesak have been recruited into that that brigade. The brigade will carry out combat activities and attempt to liberate these towns. UN representatives are also aware of the information that the commander of the 2nd Corps has been deployed in the municipality of Kladanj for a while now and that he is personally involved in the preparation for combat. There is also a suspicion that the Serbian intelligence sources have been able to break into the system of satellite connections of the United Nations and that they have information about the preparation and the carrying out of combat in these areas." This was signed by the desk officer for intelligence, Ekrem Salihovich. He's the one who sent out this document. On pages 27 and 28, you have dealt with this document. That's in Serbian, and in 25 -- on page 25 of this report, in English. Could you please tell us something about the nature of the information contained in the document that I've just quoted from? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, this is just a customary exchange of intelligence between subordinates and their superior commands. This is the necessary prerequisites -- prerequisite for the successful preparation of combat activities. Second of all, we can now be even more certain of what I have just told you and that is that the operation in question is a very significant one. The mere presence of the commander of the 2nd Corps in Kladanj and his immediate involvement in the preparations for the operation together with the Main Staff indicate the significance of that operation. Third of all, you can also see the fact that a new unit is being established and that it will involve combatants from Vlasenica and Han Pijesak, and it is really not difficult for us to tell what the axis of the operation will be and what its focus will be. The focus of the operation will be these two towns. Why is this brigade being established? Because it is to be assumed that people from these towns, future combatants from these towns, are more highly motivated to fight because they will be liberating their own home towns. This is not the first time, and this is not something that happened in the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. I have similar personal experiences, because when we carried out a counter-offensive against five corps units in 1994, my brigade was designated by the superior commands to spearhead the combat operations because they believed they were better motivated than the others coming from Bihac originally, and it was only to be expected that they would be more motivated. And morale and motivation are sometimes more important than the equipment and weapons used in conducting operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Skrbic. Can you please tell us where are the combatants from Vlasenica and Han Pijesak mentioned in this document, and where these towns are situated? In whose territory? Because probably the Trial Chamber is eager to learn all the facts.

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Combatants that are to make up the brigade are in the 2nd Corps and in some of its units. One can definitely say that they would be taken out of those units and used to form a new brigade. Han Pijesak and Vlasenica municipality were in the territory of Republika Srpska at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Skrbic. Can you please tell us, Can one see from this letter whether the commands and units of the UN deployed on the ground had intelligence information about the planned operations from Srebrenica and from other territories under ABH control?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It is completely indubitable that UNPROFOR units were aware of the preparations that this unit was making and that they were able to monitor the operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Does this intelligence report says [as interpreted] precisely that they did know that or is it just your assumption?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says here that they were fully aware.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have document 1D431 admitted into evidence. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It will be marked for identification pending translation.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Your Honour, 65 ter document 1D431 shall be assigned Exhibit D360, marked for identification pending translation. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... received on the English channel the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I will try again, Your Honours. 65 ter document 1D431 shall be assigned Exhibit D360, marked for identification pending translation. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Can we now have in e-court document P2369. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Now, can you tell us, for the record, if you dealt with this document on pages 33 and 34 in the Serbian version and on page 5 of the English version of your report. Page 30 in English. Do you recall?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us, What does this document from Bosnia-Herzegovina, dated 9th eleven -- 9th November, 1994, mean?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In military terms, the basic idea is a visualisation of the battle-ground. In other words, it is a summary of what the commander intends to achieve in the forthcoming operation. After the basic idea is set up, the staff is going to expound on the relevant decision. And I'm not going to go into the whole decision-making process, I will only say that after such a decision has been taken, this part of the basic idea can be either modified to a certain extent or remain unchanged, and it becomes paragraph four of an order or a directive.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Skrbic. Now, please, can you tell us this: Is it customary for the Main Staff of the Supreme Command of the ABiH to elaborate a basic idea for the level of the Srebrenica operations group which is lower than the corps which it is subordinated?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not a usual and standard military procedure. However, it is possible, provided the commander decides to do so. Therefore, it is not necessarily prohibited to pursue this course. But this indicates that we are talking here about a very significant operation that has a very specific objective, given that it's being prepared by the Main Staff. This document was preceded by a document from the 8th OG in which the 8 G commander -- OG commander proposed a participation of his units in the operation and proposes his own basic idea. For that reason, after reviewing this proposal from the 8th OG, the Main Staff did what they did and sent their basic idea to the 8th OG. The normal procedure would be for this idea to be forwarded to the corps first, and then the 2nd Corps command would prepare their own concept of the operation and on that basis distribute tasks to its subordinate units, including the 28th Division.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, can you please take a look at item 1, and it speaks about this idea, and I'm going to quote.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Mr. Tolimir please tell us exactly the referenced paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: "The plan is to liberate in active combat actions part of the temporarily seized territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina - the municipalities of Bratunac, Vlasenica, Sekovici, Zvornik, and Kalesija - and link the free territories of Zepa and Srebrenica with the free territories of Zvornik, Kalesija, and Zivinice in order to create a permanent free corridor for the supply of the population and logistics support to the Army of RBH and the basis for the future liberation of north-eastern Bosnia as a whole." Does this reflect the basic idea of the Supreme Command and the tasks and duties to be conferred upon units in order to implement this idea in practice?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We can clearly see what the intention of the Supreme Command is, and that is actually the purpose of the basic idea. And now one can clearly recognise what the objectives of the operation are. It is not only to liberate the temporarily occupied territories mentioned herein, but also the creation of favourable conditions and good operational basis for the continuation of combat operations and eventual liberation, as he put it, of the whole of north-eastern Bosnia. The planned operation, according to this idea and the intention highlighted by the commander, is of strategic importance for the RBH army.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, underneath, they specifically and very precisely determine both the left and right boundaries of the corridor. Can you tell us something about the corridor, and through whose territory would they run?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's part of the territory under the VRS control or, rather, part of the territory of the Republika Srpska. In this particular instance they call it a corridor, although this is not a typical corridor. This is a wide stretch of territory, and I said a minute ago that it would serve as a good operational basis for the continuation of their activities. This means that the Main Staff realised the importance of this territory and realised the importance of the size of the corridor or, if you want, of the operational basis for further operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: If we look at the border-lines on the left side and then underneath where it says "right border," and there are all the villages there named that are supposed to be linked through operations, can you tell us what is the width between the left and the right borders? How wide would this corridor would be?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since I never went to this area and I don't have a map in front of me, it is very hard for me to give you an answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. But one can see here that the left border is the one controlled by the Zepa Brigade during combat operations, too; whereas the right border starts from Brestovik, trig point 1291. Then you have the villages of Podzeplje and Brestovik. Can you tell us how far these villages are from trig point 1291?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, I believe that the distance is between 15 and 20 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: As a military expert, can you please tell us: What is the width of defence covered by a division or by a brigade? The width of its defence line. And you can choose whichever you prefer.

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A brigade defends 10 to 12 kilometres, and a division defends even over 20 kilometres of a front line.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Now, according to this basic idea, is it envisaged that a brigade and a division should occupy such territory that is normally envisaged to be defended by a brigade or a division respectively?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A unit is never tasked with an assignment that it cannot accomplish. And you never determine an area of operation that these units cannot maintain after it occupies it. That means that the brigade and the division were tasked with opening the corridor that in the forthcoming period they would be capable of defending.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Mr. Skrbic. Can you please now look at item 2 of this document, and I'm going to read it. We're going to see it on our screens. This is the next page. Item 2, the second paragraph from the top. And it reads: [As read] "How to execute the task: Liberate the temporarily seized sector of the corridor, inserting large forces into the depth of the corridor sector and engaging in offensive operations from the free territories of OG-4, OG-6, the 2nd Corps, and OG-8 Srebrenica, and afterwards secure the north-eastern and south-western side of the corridor at the lines given in item 1. "Engage the already prepared logistics support immediately through the 2nd Corps." Please, this infiltration of forces that was planned from the territory under the control of the ABiH in Central Bosnia, together with the 2nd Corps --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The accused is kindly asked to repeat the question, which was not clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, the interpreters asked you to repeat the question; they didn't understand it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I'll repeat my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Mr. Skrbic, I have quoted this. Does this show the way in which the task was carried out, according to which it was planned to infiltrate forces from the central Bosnian territory under the control of the 2nd Corps of the ABiH and from territories of the liberated zones of Srebrenica and Zepa? So were sabotage and terrorist groups infiltrated from those territories?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: "from the demilitarised zones," not "from the liberated zones."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No plans were in place for infiltrating sabotage and terrorist units. The plan was to have significant forces infiltrated from territory under the control of the ABiH army -- or, rather, from territory that was the area of responsibility of the 2nd Corps of the ABiH. It was also planned to infiltrate forces from the 28th Division from the protected zone, and they were to infiltrate the depth of the territory of Republika Srpska. As we can see, operations were reliant on those units that were to be infiltrated into the depth of the territory, because these units were expected to take advantage of the element of surprise and to ensure that other units had favourable conditions that would allow them to carry out their task.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Skrbic. Please have a look at 3, item 3, engagement of forces. And let's see what the task is for the 285th and the light brigade. 3.1. I'll quote. I'll read it out.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please scroll up the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: "The 284th East Bosnian Light Brigade used the entire 284th Eastern Bosnian Light Brigade for insertion into the depth of the corridor into the original sectors, combat group by combat group (battalion strength). Reinforce combat groups as needed from other brigades with the minimum number of soldiers for a realistic execution of the set task and keep them in the field until they link up with the other forces." My question is as follows: Did the Main Staff of the ABiH Supreme Command plan to have the whole 284th Iblbr inserted into the corridor, in the territory that was under the control of the VRS, and did they plan to have that force remain there until other forces, remaining forces, from the ABiH arrived in the area? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That just confirms what I was previously saying. It's not a matter of infiltrating sabotage and terrorist groups; it's a matter of infiltrating significant forces. The 284th Brigade was probably the most capable unit from the 28th Division. Given that, the Main Staff had planned to infiltrate this brigade, to have this brigade infiltrate territory that was under the control of the VRS. It was planned to have the entire brigade infiltrate the territory. There were supposed to be units the strength of a battalion that were to infiltrate the territory. These are strong units, especially when they infiltrate the enemy's rear. They can thus inflict very significant losses on the units in whose territory they are present.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Skrbic. Please, have you come across any documents which state that certain forces from Zepa and from Srebrenica infiltrated the territory of Republika Srpska? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I came across a number of such documents, and that confirms that there had previously been cases of infiltration but not to the extent that was now being planned. In these documents that I previously found, these prior infiltrations concerned the infiltration of sabotage and reconnaissance units, reconnaissance units the strength of a platoon. Such units had between 20 and 30 soldiers. These groups inflicted significant losses on the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. If we have a look at the engagement of forces. I won't read through the entire paragraph that relates to groups and subgroups, but is mentioned made of areas between Zepa and Srebrenica? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, those areas are also mentioned. But there is something else that I would like to add which I believe is very important, and this will enable us to have a better understanding of this operation and its purpose. If we see that the Main Staff issues tasks to a brigade and to units below the level of brigade, a brigade is three levels below the Main Staff, but in this case it's issuing tasks to combat groups formed by brigades, and even to combat subgroups. So now we're going five levels down, and this is extremely rare. But once again let me say that it is the commander's right to decide how to use certain units and also to decide who will assign tasks to these units. Since this operation is a very serious one and the purpose of the operation is very serious, the Main Staff assumed responsibility for assigning tasks to groups at such low levels. In contemporary armies, this could be tolerated more easily, because given the contemporary systems of command and control and of managing units and operations, commanders at the highest levels can have communication links and can issue tasks to groups at the level of a company. This isn't always good in terms of military doctrine, but if the commander so decides, if he decides that this is the manner in which his objective will be reached, then he has the right to proceed in this manner, because he is the commander, the authorised official, who decides who will command a unit and in what manner.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Skrbic. Could we now please have a look at A, or could you have a look at item A, which relates to the first combat group, Combat Group 1. Certain facilities are mentioned - Velja Glava, Snagovo, and Djafin Kamen. Are these places referred to?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
