utterances.text: Do these features mean anything to you? Where are they, in fact, located, Velja Glava and Snagovo, which areas? In relation to the column that was breaking through.

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These features are partially to be found on the axis of -- on the breakthrough axis of the 28th Division. They are in the territory of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Skrbic. Have a look at the second subgroup referred to under A. In the second line, is the village of Camilja [phoen] Kula Grad mentioned? And the Kula Grad fortress, is that a place mentioned in the third line?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, these places are mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please tell us where, as far as you can remember, these places are located? In the vicinity of which large settlements or towns? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say for certain which large towns they are close to, but what I can say is that they are near the Drina river. And part of the objective of the operation was that after an operations base had been established, the operation should continue and the forces should break through to the Drina river. I can also point out that these places are located in the territory of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. We saw, under the heading "idea," we saw something about the left border, and the village of Pozege [phoen] was supposed to be the first location there. Now you're mentioning the Drina river as a location that was fixed. Where is the village of Pozeplje located, could you please tell us then? And what is the distance between Pozeplje and the banks of the Drina river? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Pozeplje is in the vicinity of Zepa, but I couldn't really tell you how far it is from the river Drina.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Is the village of Pozeplje in the vicinity of the Main Staff in Han Pijesak? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It is in the vicinity of the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. And could you perhaps estimate the distance between the Main Staff and the banks of the river Drina in the area where OG-8 was active, or, rather, part of the forces from Srebrenica? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think that was a distance of about 30 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Skrbic. Given the distances and the extent of the territory that they wanted to liberate, could you tell us whether this concerns linking up territory under the control of the ABiH? Did it concern linking up that territory in Central Bosnia with territory in Eastern Bosnia, which is where these protected zones were located? In the vicinity of the Drina Rijeka, the Drina river. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can confirm that. Because this is part of the main objective, the main idea, expressed by the Main Staff. The purpose was to link up these territories, the territory under the control of the ABiH or, rather, the 2nd Corps. This territory was to be linked up with the territory of the Srebrenica and Zepa enclaves.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's have a look at item 3. It concerns the forces of the 2nd Corps of the ABiH. Thank you. 3.4.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Aleksandar. It's page 10 in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: At the bottom of this page in the Serbian language and at the bottom of the page in the English version as well, we can see it says the 2nd Corps forces of the ABiH. And it says: "The main forces of Operations Group 6 and Operations Group 4 are engaged on this task with reinforcement from other 2nd Corps complements." And then it mentions basic tasks. My question is as follows: In this complex operation planned by the Main Staff on the 9th of November, 1994, was action planned by ABiH units from Central Bosnia from the 2nd Corps in order to link up with forces with Zepa and Srebrenica? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is more than obvious. The rest of the 2nd Corps - and why do I say the rest? because the 28th Division is also on the strength of the 2nd Corps - was given a special task. They were to launch an operation on the axis from Central Bosnia to eastern enclaves.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. We don't want to go on reading the entire document. Let's look at 4.8 in this document. This is on the last page, and this was -- this will also give us an opportunity to see the opportunity [as interpreted]. In English it is page 13, the last page. Thank you. This will give us an opportunity to see the signature. 4.8. And I quote: [As read] "We have realistic information that the Chetniks are preparing to attack you, but we don't know yet when or how. Should this be the case, a troublesome defence lies in store for you in the final breakthrough from the encirclement, which is a very complex operation. Because you will have the people on your back, you will lose free territory, and you will have to move through the occupied territory. Compared to that, this operation doesn't have such significant problems. It is essential that we commence the operation before the Chetniks decide to attack. We can and indeed we will help you to break through the encirclement, but certainly on a smaller scale and less effectively than in the execution of the operation." My question is this: Did the Main Staff, or, rather, the Supreme Command of the BiH Army, know what the risks were? And despite being aware of the risks, did they decide to launch a decisive operation to pre-empt the Chetniks' attack? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not only were they aware of all that, they envisaged all that. This document clearly shows that the Main Staff of the BiH Army warns the command of the 28th Division about what they can expect about the situation that may be in store for them. This bullet point indicates that the Main Staff already had information that Srebrenica would come under attack, that it would be threatened. Not only did they have that information, they also knew that it -- Srebrenica will not be defended, because the message of the commander of the 8th Group shows that their future breakthrough from the encirclement is not as significant as the operation that was planned. It is clearly shown by the document that the Main Staff warns the command that the breakthrough is a very complex operation and that it will be even more complex for them. It will be compounded by the fact that they will have people on their backs, civilians, and that they will have to break through an occupied territory under the control of the Army of Republika Srpska - and I'm talking about the same distance of 60 kilometres that we have already mentioned. Besides that, the Main Staff warns the command of the 8th OG that the Army of Republika Srpska might carry out the so-called pre-emptive action, because the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska had intelligence to the effect of such an operation being in the pipeline. The 8th OG is warned that if their action is pre-empted by the Army Republika Srpska, they will be on their own in the breakthrough. And as you can see in the document, they say that they want to help, however, to the extent possible and to the extent matching the significance of the planned operation. Since the objective of the planned operation is much above and beyond the task of protecting and preserving Srebrenica, he spelled it out quite clearly in this bullet point and he left it to OG-8 to independently solve any problems that might arise from their decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Skrbic. And now let us look at bullet point 4.9, right underneath. And I quote: [As read] "Keep this document to yourself ... any leaks from the document will be your personal responsibility. From it, you can issue tasks in segments to those who are to carry them out. The entire operation and its objective must not be given to anyone until the specified moment and without our approval. After you study it, you may destroy it at your discretion or keep it secure and destroy it when you see fit." My question is this: Why all the secrecy measures with regard to these operations? Why do you think that all the information regarding the operation has to be so secret and confidential? What would be your opinion on that?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The objective calls for secrecy not only in this operation but by and large in all operations. This is a well-known military problem, and that is when to convey tasks to subordinated units from the superior units. In all the militaries of the world, this is an unresolved issue. Every time when a task is sent down the line to a lower unit, the danger of information leak increases. That is why commanders are very cautious whenever they are in a position to send their decisions down to subordinated units. However, there is an inherent danger in that. One may be overly cautious and as a result a decision arrives too late and subordinated units do not have enough time to prepare for the task. In this document this is very obvious. In this very bullet point this is very obvious. The commander -- or, rather, the Main Staff, here, orders how the document/documents should be treated if they contain the highest possible secret regarding the operation. That's why the commander ordered that tasks should be issued to the subordinated units in segments and that the sequence of the implementation as envisaged in the main idea should be followed. In other words, another plan will be drafted for the operation, and all the ensuing orders have to be based on that plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Skrbic. Please, you have testified that the person who gave this order also knew that the civilian population would be moving out of Srebrenica together with the troops. How did you know that? Or whose decision was it to move out the civilian population from Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. If we could have a reference to that particular statement. I didn't see it in the transcript as he's been testifying so far today, at least.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, can you give us the reference for that?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. The reference for that is under bullet point 4.9 -- or, rather, 4.8. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, you misunderstood the request of Mr. Vanderpuye. He was asking you for a reference to your statement. You said in the last question to the witness: "Mr. Skrbic, please, you have testified that the person who gave this order also knew that the civilian population would be moving out of Srebrenica together with the troops." Could you give us a reference where Mr. Skrbic testified to that effect?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. This is not what I said. I said: Since you in your answers said that they will have a problem of the population on their back, did you study how the decision was made to transfer the civilian population from Srebrenica? That was my question. And the reference about that, which was repeated by the witness, is bullet point 4.8, line 4, where it says: "You will have --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, that is sufficient. It was obviously an interpretation matter. Sir, the question of Mr. Tolimir is: Did you study how the decision was made to transfer the civilian population from Srebrenica? Could you please answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I researched that issue. And I have dealt with it in a chapter entitled: "Evacuation from Srebrenica."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, I think it's now the time for the second break. You may then proceed after the break. We will resume at 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tolimir. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I would like to call up P990. Thank you. The witness referred to that document in one of his answers. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: We see a document issued by the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. It's a municipality of Srebrenica. The presidency of that municipality has sent this document on the 9th of July, 1995, to the president of the Presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina, Mr. Alija Izetbegovic, as well as to the commander of the RBH army, Army General Rasim Delic. I quote from the report: "This is a report from the session of the Srebrenica municipality presidency held on the 9th of July, 1995, at 1900 hours. [As read] "The aggressor army entered the town at 1800 hours from the direction of Zeleni Jadar. Our military command is dissolving, and the members of the 28th Division of the ground forces are no longer able to do anything to prevent aggressor forces from entering the town. Chaos and panic are rife, and the civilian authorities are left with the last unpopular step to save the population. And it is stressed that a meeting at the level of the state and military organs of the RBH with the Serbian aggressor side, which means that a noted meeting should be set up with the Serbian aggressor side with the aim of finding a possibility to open a corridor for the population to move to the nearest free territory of the RBiH under the control of international factors. We need an urgent reply no later than 2400 hours. "President of the Presidency Osman Suljic," mining engineer. Thank you. Mr. Skrbic, could you please tell us what, Conclusions would you infer from this document?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, I have to draw your attention to the date of the document and the time when the session of the presidency of the municipality of Zepa was held, at 1900 hours. And before I share with you my final conclusions about this document, I would like to point to the fact that an urgent answer is sought no later than 24 hours. Which means that if the session started at 1900 hours, it must have lasted at least for an hour; an hour later the telegram was sent, which means that it was sent at 2000 hours; which means that only four hours remained to the highest political leadership of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina to provide their answer to the request. What does this mean? This means that the Presidency of -- the Presidency of Zepa municipality and his associate are under pressure and in a lot of haste. Second of all, on the 9th of July, 1995, the Army of Republika Srpska did not enter the urban area, which points to the following conclusion: In this way, the president of the Presidency of Zepa municipality -- I apologise, Srebrenica municipality, tries to make the situation more dramatic than necessary in order to receive an urgent answer from President Izetbegovic and commander of the Main Staff Rasim Delic. And now I will move on to the gist and the essence of the document. The gist of the document is this: For the military, i.e., the command and the troops of the 28th Division, it is true that it is in a state of chaos. If we were to strictly apply the principles of the military doctrine, one should expect that the enemy are in a state of chaos, because they will not be able to put up any meaningful resistance to our advances. Second of all, when we are talking about the civilian population, it is abundantly clear here that the civilian population and their local bosses intend to move out. And they are pleading with President Alija Izetbegovic and Commander Rasim Delic to strike an urgent deal with the Army of Republika Srpska to open the corridor for the population to move out. There is no doubt about the fact that the population of Srebrenica already on the 9th and even before that - and I will come back to that later - wanted and intended to leave the area, to move out. If we go even further back, to the year 1993, to the time when the Drina Corps carried out a counter-offensive against the 28th Division in order to return the territories that it had previously lost, until the 17th of April, 1994, already then the local civilian authorities of Srebrenica called for a similar arrangement to be made. They wanted to move out under three conditions. They were prepared to leave the area under three conditions: The first one being for the wounded to be evacuated by helicopter - if I'm not mistaken; the second condition was for the civilians to be evacuated by other means of transport; and the third condition, when all that was done, was for a corridor to be opened to allow the troops to leave in the direction of Tuzla on foot. You can find this in a report by the Secretary-General of the United Nations. I can't remember in which paragraph, but I'm sure that it exists in his report. Why did I go back? I want to show to the Trial Chamber that the idea of abandoning Srebrenica existed among the Muslims even before the 6th of July, 1995. That idea had pre-existed that date. It had pre-existed the attack on Srebrenica. And this is what I wanted to say about this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. In the last three lines of the document that we have in front of us, it says: "... finding a possibility to open a corridor for the population to move out to the nearest free territory of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina under the control of international elements." My question is as follows: Did the Srebrenica civilian authorities request that a corridor be opened from Srebrenica to territory under the control of the ABiH and the government? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Naturally. An explicit request was made to organise a meeting with the VRS and to arrange for the opening of such a corridor without fighting and in agreement with the VRS. The request was to agree on opening a corridor to the nearest stretch of territory under the control of the ABiH, and that area was the Tuzla area. As far as this stretch of territory under international control is concerned, well, this relates to moving the population out via territory under international control.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Does this mean that they had requested an evacuation of the population from Srebrenica to territory under the control of the ABiH?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One could say so, but conditionally, because evacuation has a different meaning when compared to the term "moving out." If you say "moving out," if they are requesting that the population be moved out, that means that they will move out voluntarily. And with the assistance of international elements, the population will move out. If you say "evacuation," it means that someone has to evacuate them. Someone has to go to collect them and transport them to the nearest stretch of territory under the control of the ABiH. And this should have concerned the civilian authorities from Tuzla. They would have had to go and evacuate the population with the necessary means. In this particular case, what we are dealing with is moving out population. And the term "to move out," as far as I understand that expression, means that there is no intention to return. However, in my understanding, the term "evacuation" means that when the conditions are favorable for a return, the population would return to the place they left. That is my understanding of these two different expressions.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Skrbic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please now see Exhibit D174. Thank you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Mr. Skrbic, on the screen we have before us a document from Mr. Akashi, from the UNPROFOR HQ in Zagreb, addressed to Kofi Annan, the Secretary-General of the UN. It's dated the 11th of July, 1995. If we now have a look at item 1, the first three lines of that item, this is what it says: "The purpose of this message is to inform you of plans I am making to deal with the situation in Srebrenica and to provide you with our preferred line for your approaches to the council." And then it says: "I have just concluded a meeting with my senior military and political advisors and with the UNHCR Special Envoy, at which a general consensus was reached on the policy that UNPF, UNPROFOR, and UNHCR will pursue with regard to Srebrenica in the coming one to seven days ..." Could you comment on this introduction in which Mr. Akashi is addressing Mr. Annan? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This means that Mr. Akashi, as the Secretary-General's special envoy, together with his civilian and political advisors drew up a plan stating how the UN should act in co-operation with the UNHCR. He sent the plan to the Secretary-General and waited for the UN Security Council to make its position known. This means that UN forces had a plan for dealing with the Srebrenica problem and, in particular, for dealing with the problem of the civilian population there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Skrbic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please see page 2 of the document now. Thank you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Mr. Skrbic, I'll read out part of the first paragraph now. "The UNHCR reports that 80 to 90 per cent of the population of Srebrenica (the total population is 40.000) are displaced persons who fled fighting earlier in the war, thus they do not have long-standing ties to homes and property in the enclave and will probably be interested in leaving for Tuzla. A UNHCR local staff member in Srebrenica --" I'll repeat what I said, "a UNHCR local staff member in Srebrenica reported today that virtually everyone in the enclave wishes to leave." Mr. Skrbic, in this document here, does it refer to information on the basis of which Mr. Akashi took the decision he took concerning international organisations in Srebrenica and in Bosnia? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, first of all, we can tie this up -- this position can be tied up with the previous document that we had a look at, and this position confirms what I previously said, and that is that the population of Srebrenica had the intention of moving out. Here this intention is expressed as their wish, because it quite unambiguously states that in the United Nations they believe that only some of the population wanted to go to Tuzla, but later they realised that the entire population wanted to leave the area. First it says only displaced persons and then it says everyone. This is not the only document in which this wish is expressed. There are other documents in which the wish is expressed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Skrbic. You mentioned the previous document. Are you referring to the document of the 9th that the president of Srebrenica municipality drafted after the meeting that had been held at 1800 hours? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Did UNPROFOR command in Srebrenica have such information, and UNPROFOR command in Tuzla, Sarajevo, and Zagreb as well - thank you - since a request had been made from Srebrenica for international forces to act as mediators in opening up a corridor that would allow the population to move out? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If the system of command and control in UNPROFOR was functioning correctly, then it wouldn't be realistic to expect that the UNPROFOR command in Srebrenica was unaware of these activities. That would be quite unbelievable because that command was in Srebrenica with people and that body would be the body that would first be informed about such intentions, and one would expect that body to be the first body to commit itself to finding a solution to that problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Skrbic. Let's now have a look at the second paragraph, which is the last one of this page, from page 1 in the Serbian version. And it's the second paragraph under B, the last five lines. The second paragraph under B. It says, and I quote: [As read] "The Dutch will receive instructions to remain in the Srebrenica enclave until an agreement is reached with the government of the Bosnian Serbs and until authorisation is obtained for those people to leave the enclaves. Ideally, a significant number of armed troops from UNPROFOR will remain in the enclave at least until all those who want to leave the enclave actually leave it. This option has to be harmonised with the wish of the Dutch government to evacuate its forces as soon as possible from Srebrenica. UNPROFOR will also try to reach an agreement with the Bosnian Serbs to escort any convoy of refugees from Srebrenica to Tuzla." Mr. Skrbic, bearing in mind what I have just read out, could you please tell me what you think of this? What was UNPROFOR's attitude to this? What was their position? And did Mr. Kofi Annan know what the population thought about moving out, since he's stating what role everyone will play until the population has finally moved out? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is a matter of standard procedure here that is also followed by other armies, although UNPROFOR units are United Nations units, but the chain of command is not significantly different from the chain of command in armies throughout the world. So we can see that the Dutch Battalion will be assigned a task. They will be instructed on how to act to make sure that the civilian population can move out of Srebrenica. In addition, the document also says that the Dutch government has been informed. And we can only speculate that the Dutch government is concerned for the security of their forces and they want to establish how to move their forces out of the enclave as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Skrbic. Please now have a look at item C. I'm interested in the first two sentences -- or the first sentence, in fact. It's the next page in the Serbian version, and it's on the same page in the English version, which we have in front of us. It says, under C, and I quote: "While satisfactory arrangements for the departure of refugees are being sought, UNPROFOR will negotiate the departure of Dutch troops from Srebrenica." Thank you. Please, in this document from Mr. Annan -- I apologise, from Mr. Akashi, which was sent on the 11th of July, 1995, in this document is mentioned made of seeking a solution for the refugees? And is mentioned made of the departure of the Dutch Battalion? What is your opinion of this as an expert? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, first of all, it is necessary to distinguish two questions, first of all. First of all, there is the question of Mr. Akashi's conduct in relation to his assistance and in relation to the civilians. The second question is the question of what to do with the Dutch Battalion, and here you can see the division of responsibility with regard to those two issues. As for the civilian population and as for the decision on moving the population out, it's the civilian component of UNPROFOR that is responsible for that decision. And the decision -- or, rather, the responsibility for evacuation is the responsibility of UNPROFOR command. The civilians perform their own duties, and the army performs its own duties. This is quite logical.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Skrbic. In relation to moving out the refugees in the enclave, well, was this the firm position that UNPROFOR had? When we have a look at item C that I have read out, could you say whether UNPROFOR had a firm position with regard to the departure of civilians? Or was this position one that was developed, given the way that events unfolded on the ground? Or is something else at stake? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is no doubt at all that the civilian population or refugees were going to move out. The only thing that was sought was the way how to do it and the best possible way. When that way was found, there is no doubt that the Dutch Battalion would also be evacuated, because their deployment in Srebrenica would have lost its purpose. My final conclusion is, therefore, that there is a firm position that the civilian population has to move out.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Skrbic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like the electronic court to go to the following page in the Serbian as well as in English. I'm interested in bullet point 3. I would like to thank the e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: And now I'm going to quote from the document. I'm quoting from 3(a): "UNHCR will immediately begin negotiations with the Bosnian Serbs for the provision of emergency food and medical supplies for the people in Srebrenica, particularly the wounded, and the approximately 25.000 displaced persons who had fled combat; the safe, rapid, and orderly departure from Srebrenica of all those people, including men of military age for Tuzla, beginning with the evacuation of the wounded on an emergency basis." Thank you. Please, looking at this part here, in the document sent by the Akashi, would you say that this part specifies UNHCR obligations? Look at the first sentence, where it says "UNHCR will immediately begin negotiations with the Bosnian Serbs," is this an approval for such conversations? And if somebody receives a document from the UNPROFOR command in Zagreb, would they act in accordance with such a document? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If Mr. Akashi, the special representative of the UN Secretary-General, says that UNPROFOR will immediately start negotiating with the Serbian side, that means one and only thing: This is the beginning of the implementation of the plan to move out the civilian population from Srebrenica. I recognise this as the first task given to one of the interested parties or an interested bodies which also has obligations as a humanitarian organisation. If you get such a task, that means that you start implementing a plan. Not only in this case. This would be the case in combat operations or in any other military operation. This is also the case in civilian structures, in governments, or in any organised civilian society.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Skrbic. And now let's look at the second part of the sentence, and I am going to quote from it. "The safe, rapid, and orderly departure from Srebrenica of all those people, including men of military age for Tuzla, beginning with the evacuation of the wounded on an emergency basis." Thank you. My question is this: This is an instruction provided by Mr. Akashi; does it also imply that UNHCR representatives should immediately begin these activities in order to facilitate the departure of everybody, including men of military age for Tuzla? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is no doubt about that. The only thing I can add to that is this: As you can see in the document, some priorities have been set; the first to be evacuated are the wounded, which is only normal, and the rest will follow.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to go to the following page in Serbian. The English page is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: This is in both versions in both letters. I will quote: "Our efforts to negotiate with the Bosnian Serbs and to ameliorate the situation on the ground would potentially be greatly facilitated if the council were to make several points on an urgent basis, preferably in the form of a resolution, but alternatively in the form of a presidential statement." And then under (e) it is stated, and I quote: "All those who wish to leave Srebrenica should be allowed to do so under the protection of UNHCR." My question is this: Could you please explain something about this document: Whose was the decision for the population of Srebrenica to move out? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, the decision was not taken as such, but it was in the pipeline and it will be taken. The second thing that I would like to highlight here is the fact that this document clearly shows that in complex situations it is not easy to reach a decision. Even people with the highest diplomatic credibility, such was Mr. Akashi, had a hard time making a decision, which is clearly seen from the first paragraph that you read out. Mr. Akashi needed support in the form of a resolution, or at least a presidential notification from the Security Council. I repeat: It's very difficult to make a decision, and it's always easier for the top executive to make such a decision. And that is true of both the military as well as civilian structures.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Skrbic. Would such a top executive make decisions based on the information that he receives from his subordinates? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody makes decisions without information. The information in question has to be relevant for the decision to be good, for the decision to be implementable, with the least effort, and in the most cost-effective way. Whoever makes a decision has to have information, not only from his subordinates, and in this case it is more pronounced than in normal conditions in the army because the subordinates are far away from the decision-maker. It has the right information that may be provided to the Secretary-General, and if the Secretary-General makes a decision, it will be a good support for Mr. Akashi at the moment when he wants to implement his plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Skrbic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I think the time has come for the Court to rise. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You are right, Mr. Tolimir. We have to adjourn the for the day, and we will resume tomorrow morning at 9.00 in this courtroom. And again, this advice: No contact to other party during the break, please. We adjourn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 8th day of February, 2012, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.47 p.m.,
